title: Linear-time minimization of deterministic finite automata
formal: For every fixed integer a≥2, is there a deterministic word-RAM algorithm that minimizes every complete n-state DFA over [a] in O(n) worst-case time?
definitions: Use a uniform word-RAM with word length w, addressed word memory, addition and subtraction modulo 2^w, multiplication modulo 2^w, Boolean bit operations, shifts by less than w, comparisons and conditional branches, each costing one step. Lower bounds for a particular partition-refinement framework do not establish a lower bound for every such algorithm. The unary-alphabet special case does not resolve the fixed alphabet of size at least two.

title: Strassen’s asymptotic rank conjecture for concise cubic tensors
formal: For every n≥1 and every tensor T∈ℂ^n⊗ℂ^n⊗ℂ^n whose three flattenings all have rank n, is lim_{k→∞} R(T^⊗k)^(1/k)=n?
definitions: R(T) is the least r such that T=Σ_{i=1}^r a_i⊗b_i⊗c_i with a_i,b_i,c_i∈ℂ^n. Each flattening views the tensor as a linear map from the dual of one factor into the tensor product of the other two. In T^⊗k the first, second and third tensor factors are respectively grouped, producing a tensor with three factors ℂ^(n^k). Submultiplicativity of rank makes the displayed limit equal to inf_{k≥1} R(T^⊗k)^(1/k). This is exact rank over ℂ, not border rank, and there is no explicitness or computational requirement on T.

context_blocks.text: Matrix rank has a simple algebraic characterization, whereas tensor rank changes substantially when many independent copies are considered jointly. Strassen’s conjecture says that in the asymptotic setting the three flattening dimensions already determine the answer.

The cubic concise formulation is the target proposed in the personal list. It includes matrix-multiplication tensors, so a positive resolution would imply matrix multiplication exponent two; the reverse implication is not claimed. The 2024–2026 source studies structural properties of asymptotic rank without proving this equality.

title: Fixed-parameter tractability of graph isomorphism by rank-width
formal: Do a computable function f:ℕ→ℕ, an absolute constant c and a deterministic algorithm exist which decide isomorphism of graphs G,H in time f(k)(|V(G)|+|V(H)|+2)^c, where k=max(rw(G),rw(H))?
definitions: Graphs are finite simple undirected graphs given by adjacency matrices. Isomorphism is a vertex bijection preserving adjacency. For a graph G and X⊆V(G), the cut-rank is the rank over the two-element field of the adjacency submatrix with rows X and columns V(G)∖X. A rank decomposition is a tree of maximum degree three whose leaves are bijectively labeled by V(G). Every tree edge partitions the leaves and hence defines a cut-rank; the decomposition width is the maximum of those ranks. Rank-width rw(G) is the minimum width, with rw(G)=0 for at most one vertex. No decomposition or parameter value is supplied to the algorithm. The exponent c is independent of the rank-width.

context_blocks.text: Rank-width measures graph complexity through low-rank adjacency cuts and supports many structural algorithms. Graph isomorphism on bounded rank-width is tractable at each fixed width, but that does not by itself yield one exponent independent of the parameter.

Neuen’s 2026 survey identifies the remaining parameterized isomorphism frontiers. An n^{g(k)} algorithm or a quasipolynomial dependence involving n does not establish fixed-parameter tractability. The target concerns testing isomorphism, without additionally demanding canonization.

title: Does ETH imply Gap-ETH?
formal: Does the deterministic Exponential Time Hypothesis imply the deterministic Gap Exponential Time Hypothesis for sparse 3-CNF formulas?
definitions: For a 3-CNF formula F with n variables, let val(F) be the maximum fraction of clauses simultaneously satisfiable. The ETH convention here asserts that there is c>0 for which no deterministic algorithm decides satisfiability of all 3-CNF formulas in time O(2^(cn) poly(L)), where L is the binary encoding length. Gap-ETH asserts that there exist constants B≥1, δ∈(0,1) and c′>0 for which no deterministic algorithm in time O(2^(c′n) poly(L)) distinguishes val(F)=1 from val(F)≤1−δ on formulas with at most Bn clauses. Its inputs are promised to satisfy one of those two alternatives. Empty formulas are satisfiable. All constants are fixed independently of F; randomized versions are not asserted.

context_blocks.text: ETH concerns exact satisfiability, while Gap-ETH postulates comparable exponential hardness even when unsatisfiable inputs violate a fixed fraction of clauses. Their equivalence would unify many exact and approximation lower-bound assumptions.

Bitansky and coauthors distinguish ETH from the stronger gap hypothesis while obtaining exponential hardness for particular approximation tasks. Hardness for those tasks does not imply a gap-preserving sparse 3-CNF statement. This implication is distinct from asking whether either hypothesis is true.
